title: Residue relation with nonvanishing leading coefficient
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $B$ a commutative $R$-algebra, $x\in B$, $S=R[x]\subset B$, and $m$ a maximal ideal of $S$. There is a polynomial $p\in R[X]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] of positive degree such that the image in $S$ of its leading coefficient does not belong to $m$, and $p(x)\in m$. No domain, normality or Nagata hypothesis is needed.

proof.text: Contract m to n in R and embed A=R/n in the field k=S/m. Extend this embedding across F=Frac(A). The finite-type R-algebra k is also finite type over F by restriction-of-scalars descent of generators. Apply Zariski's lemma to get Module.Finite F k.

Mathlib IsFractionRing.comap_isAlgebraic_iff makes k algebraic over A. Take a nonzero q over A annihilating the image of x. Its degree is positive by natDegree_pos_of_aeval_root and the injective map A -> k. Polynomial.exists_natDegree_eq_of_mem_lifts lifts q to p over R of the same degree. The equality on the coefficient at this degree shows that the leading coefficient of p is nonzero modulo n. Evaluation commutes with the quotient map, so p(x) is in m. These are the explicit Lean coefficient and evaluation calculations.

lean.statement: theorem exists_monogenic_residue_leading_relation (R : Type u) (B : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing B] [Algebra R B] (x : B) (m : Ideal (Algebra.adjoin R ({x} : Set B))) [m.IsMaximal] : ∃ p : Polynomial R, 0 < p.natDegree ∧ algebraMap R (Algebra.adjoin R ({x} : Set B)) p.leadingCoeff ∉ m ∧ Polynomial.aeval (⟨x, Algebra.subset_adjoin (Set.mem_singleton x)⟩ : Algebra.adjoin R ({x} : Set B)) p ∈ m
